blocks.value: **Note the case labels: `REGULAR`, not `Size.REGULAR`.** Inside a switch on an enum, the type is already known, and qualifying the constant is a **compile error**. This trips up almost everyone once.
This is also the answer to a question from Lesson 6, where the list of switch-compatible types omitted `enum`. This is that omission, filled in.
A switch over an enum is one of the few places where omitting `default` is reasonable, the compiler can see every possible value. Add one anyway if constants might be added later.
Since Java 14 a `switch` over an enum can use arrows and produce a value. There is no `break`, and the compiler checks that every constant is covered:
